name: sandbox-mode-vocabulary-and-per-call-policy
what: The confinement vocabulary is a closed three-value union SandboxMode = 'read-only' | 'workspace-write' | 'danger-full-access' (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts:29) carried per capability call as SandboxExecutionPolicy { mode, workspaceRoot, sessionId? }, never fixed on the provider. SandboxPolicyService (ctx.sandboxPolicy) resolves one policy per call at packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:163-170 with the precedence approved explicit mode > the session's last 'sandbox/mode' override (overrideOf, line 177) > the deployment default ('read-only' is the schema default, line 112), and the workspace root is the canonical session cwd or the configured fallback. The provider treats the policy as fully specified (SandboxProvider.confine is abstract) and refuses to run unconfined: SandboxUnavailableError carries code SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE (index.ts:124-144).
invariants: Mode is resolved per call from the calling session; two consumers may confine under different policies at the same instant (index.ts:61-68).
Precedence is fixed: approved escalation grant > session sandbox/mode event > deployment default.
The abstract seam forbids silent unconfined passthrough: confine must return enforcing argv or fail closed (index.ts:152-157).
constants: default deployment mode: 'read-only' (Config schema default, sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:112)

name: platform-runner-chain-selection-and-probing
what: LocalSandboxProvider selects the platform's runner chain first and probes second: PLATFORM_CHAINS is linux ['bwrap','landlock'], darwin ['seatbelt'], win32 ['windows-acl'] (packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts:159-166). A sole candidate is selected with no probe and a static enforcement claim (STATIC_ENFORCEMENT: bwrap/landlock/seatbelt 'full', 'windows-acl' 'partial' because WRITE_RESTRICTED must retain Everyone and NTFS hard links alias one file object, lines 177-187); a multi-candidate chain is arbitrated once, in order, by functional probes that actually apply the read-only profile and run 'true' (defaultProbeBwrap:68-74, defaultProbeSeatbelt:85-91, landlock probe report full-vs-partial:519-539). No chain or no passing candidate yields 'unavailable', and selectRunner throws SandboxUnavailableError before anything spawns (492-510).
invariants: Selection is by platform first; probing only arbitrates among competing candidates, it never re-validates a choice that has no alternative.
The chain verdict is cached for the provider lifetime (selectedRunner, line 265/493), so probes run at most once.
An operator-supplied runnerCommand is an assertion of full enforcement and skips built-in selection and probing (317-324).
constants: probeTimeoutMs default 5_000, validated as a positive finite number because spawnSync({timeout:0}) means unbounded (index.ts:255, 194-198)
Landlock launcher failure exit code comes from LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT and is documented as versioned exit-125 (index.ts:233-237)

name: per-runner-profile-synthesis-and-writable-roots
what: Each rung expresses one policy in its own dialect: bwrapProfileArgs emits '--ro-bind / /', '--dev /dev', '--unshare-pid', '--proc /proc', '--die-with-parent' and, under workspace-write, '--tmpfs /tmp' plus a read-write bind of the workspace root (packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/profiles.ts:16-23); landlockProfileArgs builds readOnly ['/'] with readWrite ['/dev/null'] extended by '/tmp' and the workspace root (30-36); seatbeltProfileArgs emits an SBPL profile '(allow default) (deny file-write*)' plus literal /dev/null and subpath allows for the shared writable roots (51-58). The workspace-write allow-list itself has one home: writableRoots() in packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts:52-55 returns the canonical, deduplicated set [workspaceRoot, '/tmp', os.tmpdir()] and [] under read-only, so the Seatbelt grant and the in-process fs fence cannot drift apart. canonicalPath uses realpathSync.native and returns the as-spelled path when resolution fails, matching nothing until the root exists (30-41).
invariants: read-only yields an empty writable-root list; nothing but required sinks such as /dev/null is writable.
Roots are canonical before comparison, because Seatbelt filters and the fs fence both match resolved paths (/tmp IS /private/tmp on darwin).
bwrap and Landlock keep their own grant spellings (ephemeral /tmp mount, launcher flags); only Seatbelt and the fs fence share writableRoots().

name: windows-acl-write-restricted-token
what: The win32 backend mints a WRITE_RESTRICTED token via CreateRestrictedToken with flags DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | LUA_TOKEN | WRITE_RESTRICTED and a mode-selected restricting-SID list: read-only = [logon SID, Everyone]; workspace-write = [logon SID, Everyone, workspace write SID, optional private-temp write SID] (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/token.ts:196-222). It is a write-only boundary by construction: the module documents that reads, network and process visibility are NOT restricted (WRITE_RESTRICTED intersects only write accesses), console isolation is unavailable, and only ACL-addressable writes are governed (index.ts:23-39). Every Win32 call is checked and any failure throws with the API name and code, so a child is never spawned unrestricted; setTokenDefaultDaclGrant merges one full-access ACE for a restricting SID into the token default DACL so newly created objects (anonymous stdio pipes) pass the pass-2 check while creation stays gated by the parent container (token.ts:112-145, called at index.ts:294).
invariants: The restricting list is mode-selected: read-only carries no capability SID, so a standing workspace grant ACE from an earlier workspace-write period stays inert (token.ts:166-186).
Everyone remains in both lists for process initialization; that ambient surface is the documented partial-enforcement boundary, so the rung must never advertise 'full'.
Any Win32 failure throws before spawn; silent unrestricted execution is forbidden (index.ts:338-347).
constants: restricting list: 2 SIDs under read-only, 3-4 under workspace-write (token.ts:204-208)
default-DACL ACE rights: GRANT_ACCESS with FILE_ALL_ACCESS (token.ts:126-131)

name: windows-acl-capability-sid-grant-lifecycle
what: Write capability is an identity, not a path list: workspaceWriteSid derives a deterministic S-1-4-x-y SID from sha256 of the canonical workspace path (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/workspace-sid.ts:35-40) so the workspace-root ACE materializes once per workspace per machine and later provisions hit the exact-ACE skip; tempWriteSid domain-separates a private temp directory's identity with a third subauthority '-1' (49-53), so sibling sessions sharing a workspace cannot enter one another's temp trees. AclWriteGrant records standing paths (never revoked, the cross-session reuse cache) separately from revocable paths (revoked on dispose) (grant.ts:74-77, 85-103); LocalSandboxProvider holds one standing workspace grant per workspace and one revocable private-temp capability per live session/workspace pair keyed by JSON.stringify([sessionId, workspaceRoot]) (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:273-274, 392-443), creating the temp dir with mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-')) and revoking temp ACEs plus removing temp dirs at provider dispose while reporting rather than throwing cleanup failures (454-477).
invariants: Workspace and temp write SIDs must be distinct, and the private temp directory must be disjoint from every writable directory (index.ts:208-210, path-boundary.ts:34-39); the temp root must also be outside the workspace (path-boundary.ts:22-26).
A fresh provider always chooses a new random temp path, so crash residue cannot collide with or authorize a resumed session (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:379-391, 445-453).
The ambient temp root is never granted implicitly (index.ts:64-67).
constants: private temp directory prefix: 'dsh-' under os.tmpdir() (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:415)

name: escalation-ladder-and-approval-choreography
what: One strictly-wider table, WIDER_MODES, defines what a call may escalate to: read-only -> [workspace-write, danger-full-access], workspace-write -> [danger-full-access] (packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts:28-31); ESCALATION_TARGETS is the closed schema-facing vocabulary (41). validateEscalationArgs enforces that sandbox_permissions and justification travel together and the justification is a non-empty sentence (51-61). approveEscalation runs the ordered fail-closed sequence before anything executes: strict widening against the call's EFFECTIVE mode, approver composed, agent present to route the ask, then approver.request({...}) whose four outcomes map to the granted mode or four distinct verbatim throws (157-188). The model-facing texts are shared too: sandboxDenialMarker(mode) and escalationHintMarker(subject) (71-86). Production callers are the enforcing tool families: FsSandboxController.resolvePolicy builds the escalation request from ctx.approval and the exec agent/callId/signal and re-stamps the wider mode onto exactly one call (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:87-108), and its mapError wraps a FS_SANDBOX_DENIED into the marker plus same-turn hint (124-130).
invariants: Strict widening is checked at EXECUTION against the per-call effective mode, never baked into a tool schema (the schema enum is the registry-global closed target vocabulary).
A non-widening request never prompts a human; it throws before the approval channel is consulted.
A grant is one-shot: the returned mode is stamped onto the one call that asked.

name: shell-confinement-wrap-and-denial-classification
what: SandboxBashExecutor extends LocalBashExecutor and wraps the exact argv through ctx.sandbox.confine(['bash','-c',command], policy) for any confined mode, running unfenced only under danger-full-access (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:89-115, 179-181); the pwsh twin mirrors it call-for-call over ['pwsh', ...] (packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/index.ts:52-57). Each process's wrap facts (mode, enforcement, denialSignatures, runnerFailureRules, runnerProgram, workdir) are retained per ShellProcess so overlapping calls cannot be classified against another wrap (index.ts:53-66, 136-144). Classification distinguishes the two failure meanings: a runner failure means the command never ran and outranks denial — foreground calls throw SandboxUnavailableError and background processes carry runnerFailed (108-114, 151-166) — while a denial (nonzero exit plus the backend's own stderr dialect) sets sandbox.denied. isRunnerSpawnFailure attributes ENOENT/EACCES to the runner only when error.path equals argv[0] (or is absent and the syscall names it) and the caller-owned workdir is independently usable (helpers.ts:39-53), and classifyRunnerFailure requires a nonzero exit, the rule's optional exit-code gate, and a fatal signature on a line that is not an informational exclusion (81-103).
invariants: runner failure (command did not run) outranks denial (confinement worked and blocked) because they call for different retries.
Only the selected backend's own denial dialect is matched, never a cross-backend union, so a denial is never claimed that a backend cannot produce.
Confinement facts are per process, never a shared latest-wrap value.
constants: runner-failure rules per rung: bwrap 'bwrap: '; landlock exit-gated on LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT with informational line 'partial enforcement (older Landlock ABI)'; seatbelt 'sandbox-exec: '; windows-acl exit-gated 127 on 'windows-acl-run: ' (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:231-240)

denial signatures: bwrap ['read-only file system'], landlock ['permission denied'], seatbelt ['operation not permitted'], windows-acl ['access is denied','access to the path','permission denied'] (sandbox-local/src/index.ts:205-213)

name: fs-mutation-containment-fence
what: SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem but adds a per-call policy fence on the two mutations only — writeText and editText both route through checkedTarget, while reads pass through untouched because every mode permits reading (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:1-27, 80-109). read-only denies with FsError code FS_SANDBOX_DENIED; workspace-write re-canonicalizes NOW (resolve realpaths the deepest existing ancestor), requires containment under a root from writableRoots(policy) via isPathUnder, and delegates the mutation with THAT fresh target so the checked identity is the mutated one; danger-full-access delegates unfenced (122-144). The module states plainly that this is containment in trusted code over a model-controlled path, not a kernel boundary, and that the residual TOCTOU (an ancestor symlink swapped between re-check and syscall) is narrowed and accepted for this threat model; kernel-grade isolation of untrusted code stays ctx.shell's job. isPathUnder tries a lexical fast path and, when spellings differ, walks existing ancestors comparing dev+ino identity so Windows 8.3 aliases and casing are recognized without weakening containment to a textual approximation (containment.ts:58-75).
invariants: Only the two mutations are fenced; read paths are never gated.
The policy check and the mutation use the same freshly canonicalized target (no check-here-write-there).
A denial is a structured FsError with code FS_SANDBOX_DENIED, which the tool layer maps to the shared model-facing marker.
constants: missing-path stat codes tolerated by containment: ENOENT, ENOTDIR (containment.ts:12)

name: approval-service-policy-and-audit-pair
what: ApprovalService (ctx.approval) applies a session policy BEFORE any answerer sees the ask: ApprovalPolicy 'ask' delegates to the composed waterfall, 'never' resolves every ask deterministically to 'rejected' inside the service — deliberately not as a listener, because a listener registered ahead of a gate could not keep that promise (packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts:50-63, 252-266). request() requires an open turn and appends the audit pair approval/asked then approval/decided so both are enclosed by the durable log's commit boundary; an idle ask throws before appending anything (207-226). decide() races the scoped 'approval/request' waterfall against the caller's signal: an aborted signal yields 'cancelled' and discards a late answer, a missing or throwing answerer yields 'unavailable', and a rogue non-vocabulary return is normalized to 'unavailable' (258-298). The model learns the policy through a system-prompt context section plus a queued change notice from setPolicy (154-166, 176-187).
invariants: 'allowed-once' is the only grant; every other path fails closed.
The asked/decided pair must be turn-enclosed; a bare event between turns is crash-tail garbage and is refused.
The 'never' policy is decided before dispatch so registration order cannot defeat it.

name: permission-preset-bundling-and-knob-write-path
what: PermissionPresetService presents user-facing presets over two independent knobs (sandbox mode and approval policy) without merging them: the built-in table defaults to {'workspace-write': workspace-write + ask, 'danger-full-access': danger-full-access + never} (packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/index.ts:164-181). A switch records one 'permission/preset' event then writes only the changed knobs through their canonical setters setSandboxMode/setApprovalPolicy (379-396), and the derived state 'custom' is display-only and can never name a table entry or be a switch target (73, 192-194). The service refuses to compose over an unconfined executor by checking ctx.shell.sandboxMode, and it pins missing permission facts for every session at creation so a fresh session has a durable preset, sandbox mode and approval policy (195-197, 404-429). The read side is the 'permissions' session projection (stateVersion 2) carrying the whole select value; the write side is the /permission command, and a settings section named 'permission' holds the default preset for future sessions (211-223, 237-244, 255-275).
invariants: Execution, prompt narration and replay keep reading the knob folds; the preset event only preserves user intent when two presets share a bundle.
The name 'custom' is reserved and cannot be configured as a preset.
Composing presets over an executor that does not confine is a load-time misconfiguration, not a runtime fallback.

name: session-sandbox-mode-override-log
what: A session's sandbox-mode override is stored in its own log: setSandboxMode appends exactly one 'sandbox/mode' event and nothing mutates mode state out of band (packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/src/session-mode.ts:44-55). The event is log-only — durable and replayable, never in the model transcript — and source:'delegation' marks an override seeded into a child (24-39). SandboxPolicyService registers the fold as the 'sandboxMode' session projection (stateVersion 1) whose apply returns event.data.mode, so effective mode = projection state ?? deployment default and an override survives restart by replay with no external config store (sandbox-policy/src/index.ts:132-138, 177-179). The same resolved policy is contributed to the cache-safe runtime-context snapshot so replay reconstructs the mode the enforcing consumers resolved (index.ts:140-151, renderPolicyContext 41-55), and a package-owned invariant companion rejects any logged sandbox/mode carrying an unknown mode (invariant.ts:18-20).
invariants: The switch IS its event: the log is the only store, no external config, and two sessions can never see each other's state.
Last event wins; the fold never applies the deployment default itself.
Every logged mode must be a member of SANDBOX_MODES.

name: hooks-as-permission-gates
what: Hooks intercept tool and prompt boundaries and fold into one most-restrictive decision: mergeHookOutputs ranks deny/block 3, ask 2, approve/allow 1 and resolves deny > ask > allow, keeps the first continue:false sticky, joins only the winning rank's reasons, and accumulates additionalContext/systemMessage in hook order (packages/hooks/hook-protocol/src/merge.ts:34-99). Matching is dialect-aware — Claude word/pipe patterns are literal alternatives and everything else is an unanchored regex, Codex treats every non-empty pattern as an unanchored regex, and an invalid regex is a non-match at runtime while config parsers reject it with a diagnostic (matcher.ts:37-64). runHook executes through ctx.shell with the hook's timeoutSec (wire unit: seconds) overriding the bridge's defaultTimeoutMs, which defaults to DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000; an infrastructure rejection becomes an outcome with no exit code, so a hook that cannot run never crashes the calling turn (runner.ts:20, 67-105). The Claude Code bridge maps PreToolUse -> {kind:'deny'|'ask'} on tools/pre-execute, PostToolUse -> block, UserPromptSubmit -> reject, and a blocking Stop hook steers another step; updatedInput and systemMessage are logged and ignored, and merged.stop has no run-level halt yet (TODO) (hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:174-179, 188, 222-276). The Codex bridge honors deny only, for PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop (hooks-codex/src/index.ts:223-230).
invariants: Permission precedence is deny > ask > allow and never depends on hook registration order.
A hook infrastructure failure is a non-blocking outcome (no exit code), while a hook that DOES answer deny/ask is honored as a gate.
Hook runs inherit the agent's session workspace as cwd and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and a hookSpecificOutput block naming a different event is discarded.

name: client-approval-and-permission-surfaces
what: The browser half answers the host approval waterfall and drives permission switches, both over the Remote plane rather than a slash-command surface. ui-approval subscribes with ctx.remote.$on('approval/request'), wraps the request in a PendingApproval with a one-shot render key, registers it as a pending interaction and renders it as a conversation.composer takeover whose only outcomes are 'allowed-once' and 'rejected' (packages/client/ui-approval/src/client/index.ts:35-68, 90-92; ApprovalPanel.tsx:26-29); an unanswered request delegates to the next waterfall listener, and a signal abort settles it so a late answer is discarded (contract/slots.ts:122-159). ui-permission-presets decorates the host /permission command as a popupSelect reading the session's 'permissions' projection, marks the current value, filters the derived 'custom' state out of the pick targets, and attaches an explicit confirmation gate to the FULL_ACCESS_PRESET 'danger-full-access' row; a pick submits '/permission <preset>' so the host command remains the single write path (ui-permission-presets/src/client/index.ts:59-79, 145-166; presentation.ts:4). Its General-settings row separately writes the default preset for sessions created later through the host Settings API (index.ts:125-143).
invariants: Only one-shot decisions cross the client boundary: the UI cannot express 'always allow'.
The picker exists exactly while the host projection does; otherwise the bare invocation falls through to the host command.
The Full access preset always carries an explicit risk confirmation before the switch is submitted.

name: human-question-tool-seam
what: The ask_user_question tool is a model-facing Consumer of ctx.userQuestions: it registers a tool whose required input is an array of {id, question, header?, options?, multi_select?} and whose output is {answers:[{id, selected[], custom?}]}, mapping the wire naming (multi_select -> multiSelect) in execute (packages/interaction/tool-ask-user/src/index.ts:19-100). It passes the calling agent and the tool-execution signal into ctx.userQuestions.ask and feeds the human answer back as an ordinary tool result, so the loop pauses while a UI provider answers (80-99). The underlying seam is fail-closed: an aborted signal throws UserQuestionError ASK_ABORTED, an empty question list is refused, and a supplied agent that is not the registry's exact live runtime root throws CALLER_NOT_LIVE / DELEGATED_CALLER so an owned child with no human answerer cannot block forever (packages/interaction/user-questions/src/index.ts:41-47, 70-90).
invariants: The tool never fabricates an answer: the result is the provider's answer or a structured error.
Human interaction is valid only for the exact live runtime root, not for durable session lineage.

name: advisory-repeat-tool-guard
what: repeat-tool-reminder is an advisory per-agent repeat-call detector, not a gate: it observes on tools/post-execute, counts consecutive identical calls per agent in a WeakMap keyed by JSON.stringify([toolName, canonicalizedArguments]) where canonicalization deep-sorts JSON keys, and at each configured threshold injects a user-role reminder sourced as a plugin notice (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:189-207). It always delegates with next() and folds its reminder onto whatever the downstream decision was — a blocked call still gets the nudge — so it never vetoes or rewrites a call (209-224), and an agent/pre-step carrying a user message deletes the chain because repetition across an interjection is not a loop (226-232). Config is fail-loud at load: thresholds must be non-empty, integers >= 2, duplicate-free (normalized ascending, with thresholds[0] the gentle tier), and argumentsPreviewChars must be an integer >= 1 (128-141, 169-171). Only the model-visible preview is truncated; the chain key always compares the full canonical string (118-121).
invariants: Observe-and-enrich, never veto: counting happens first (state advances regardless of the downstream outcome), then the guard delegates and only prepends context.
Untracked calls (include/exclude wildcards) are transparent: they neither count nor reset.
A denied call still counts, because ToolRuntime routes denials through the same post-execute pipeline.

name: preset-scope-isolation-gate
what: mountPreset is the gate that keeps a per-agent preset composition from changing process-global behaviour: it refuses to mount into an unscoped context because 'its registrations would apply to every agent in the process' (packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts:378-385), then, after await() settles, it fails the mount if any row did not activate (403-406) and rejects any row that published a process-global service, telling the author to put it behind an `isolate` realm or move it to the host composition (407-413). The subtree is owned by the agent's fiber so it unwinds with the agent and a rejection leaves nothing mounted (369-376, 415-424). This is the constraint that stops a preset row from re-registering host-global capabilities such as the sandbox provider, filesystem or approval service for the whole process.
invariants: A preset mounts only into a scoped agent context; an unscoped mount is refused before anything is created.
A row that publishes a process-global service fails the whole mount instead of leaking into the host realm.
A rejected mount disposes its subtree, so failure is not partially applied.
